article.name: CrewAI
article.summary: CrewAI is a Python agent and workflow framework with an optional unified memory API, LLM-assisted memory encoding and consolidation, and shallow or adaptive-depth recall over pluggable vector storage. This is a pinned source review; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for autonomous multi-agent Crews and event-driven Flows. Its optional unified Memory API is a standalone component that can also be shared through crews, agents, and flows.

identity.text: The curated catalog resolves ordinal 171 to CrewAI, slug crewai, and explicit listed locator https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI; the pinned Atlas record is attribution only. Official GitHub API metadata identifies main as default and reports head ba2bd50f70069e3079eed29bb9cbed3f777c548b. Read-only git ls-remote and a shallow checkout matched. Reviewed 2026-11-25T10:07:39Z (UTC; 2026-11-25 02:07:39 PST; America/Los_Angeles).

architecture.text: The optional unified Memory class exposes the same store to standalone scripts and Crew, Agent, and Flow integrations. Crews can share one backing instance; agents can receive their own memory or a scoped view.

MemoryRecord stores text, ID, hierarchical scope, categories, arbitrary metadata, importance, creation/access times, optional embedding, source string, and private flag. MemoryMatch adds score, match reasons, and optional evidence-gap text.

The default backend is LanceDB; Qdrant Edge and custom StorageBackend implementations are supported. The default embedder is OpenAI unless configured; the official guide gives a local default storage path and describes embedding-dimension migration concerns.

Recall combines semantic similarity, recency decay, and importance. Configurable encoding and recall flows use LLM analysis and vector embeddings; these source-visible mechanisms do not establish measured retrieval quality.

behavior.text: Write: remember() synchronously waits on a serialized save queue; remember_many() queues batch processing in the background, and later recall drains pending writes. Encoding embeds a batch, drops near duplicates, searches for similar records, infers missing fields, requests LLM consolidation actions, and applies updates/deletions and inserts.

Update/correction: update(record_id, ...) replaces selected fields under the same ID and recomputes the vector if content changes. The record schema exposes no prior-value revision ledger. LLM consolidation can also replace or delete entries; no human review is required by this save path.

Deletion: forget() supports scope, category, age, metadata, and record-ID filters; reset() and reset_all() clear a scope or store. Backend source implements deletion, but no physical-erasure assurance or post-delete behavior was tested.

Retrieval: shallow recall performs a direct vector search and composite re-ranking. Deep recall may distill longer queries into subqueries, select candidate scopes, search in parallel, and perform a bounded deeper exploration when confidence is low. Results include match reasons and may include query-gap text; no answer-level citation or abstention guarantee was established.

Scope isolation: hierarchical scopes, root_scope, MemoryScope/MemorySlice, and private/source filters constrain searches when callers supply them. They are not authenticated identity or tenant enforcement. LanceDB uses a string-prefix LIKE filter; Qdrant Edge matches ancestor-path values. No cross-scope runtime probes were run.

Provenance/evidence: source, categories, metadata, and evidence_gaps can describe a record or retrieval gap, but source is free-form and the schema does not require document IDs, immutable supporting passages, trust state, or claim-to-source verification.

Efficiency/observability: batch embedding, intra-batch cosine deduplication, concurrent similar-record lookups and LLM analyses, candidate oversampling, and parallel recall searches are implemented. Save/query events carry success/failure and elapsed time; some event payloads include query, content, metadata, or results. No performance or cost measurements were collected.

limits.text: The bounded review covered the pinned README and memory guide, record/config types, unified Memory API, encoding and recall flows, LLM analysis, both built-in backends, scope views, backend contract, and event models. It did not trace every integration, migration, custom backend, or error path.

No system, tests, or benchmarks were run. Retrieval quality, correction behavior, deletion guarantees, actual isolation under an application policy, operating reliability, latency, cost, and storage use remain unknown.
